name: tmasjc/airbnb-market-data
what_it_holds: Repo ships pre-loaded listings.csv data for Berlin and Vienna (Vienna snapshots spanning roughly March-September 2017, ~1.1-1.3MB each) sourced from Inside Airbnb, plus a command-line downloader that can pull listings.csv for dozens of additional Inside Airbnb metro areas (amsterdam, antwerp, asheville, athens, austin, barcelona, boston, brussels, chicago, copenhagen, denver, and more per the tool's help text). 43 commits.
why_useful: Committed 2017-vintage Vienna/Berlin snapshots pre-date our held Dec-2022+ panel (gap #1), and the bundled multi-city downloader is a ready-made, low-effort tool for pulling Inside Airbnb's currently-live archive across many markets we don't yet hold.
geography: Vienna, Berlin committed; dozens more via downloader
time_coverage: 2017 (Vienna); download tool covers current live IA archive

A reusable, generic method to pull whatever historical snapshots Inside Airbnb still exposes for a given city/date, which could be pointed at any surviving NYC dates near the LL18 window or used as a template for building a systematic archive puller; not NYC-specific itself.

The CLI's historical-snapshot indexing is a possible mechanism for pulling Inside Airbnb vintages older than the ~1-year CDN retention window we're currently limited to (2017-era snapshots referenced) — directly relevant to gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps, pre-2023, including the NYC Local-Law-18 gap window). Needs verification of what host download_csv.R actually hits (may just be pointing at Wayback-cached Inside Airbnb URLs).

name: University of Glasgow — Airbnb raw scraped data collection
what_it_holds: External (non-GitHub, university data repository) archive: daily-scraped Airbnb property characteristics, booking-calendar updates, booking policies, host info and reviews for 30 Scottish Travel-to-Work Areas + 10 UK locations, June 2021-Dec 2023 monthly-aggregated occupancy/visitor/income estimates at MSOA/Intermediate Zone level, DOI 10.5525/gla.researchdata.2056. Access restricted to UBDC staff for non-commercial academic use (not freely downloadable), but methodology and code (see ubdc-airbnb above) are open.
why_useful: Documents exactly what a daily-calendar STR occupancy/income reconstruction looks like at sub-city geography (relevant to gap #2), even though we cannot pull the underlying files ourselves; worth citing as an existence proof and methodology reference, and as a reason to ask a human whether an academic-access request is worth pursuing before the pitch deadline (unlikely to clear in time).
license: University of Glasgow copyright; academic-only, gated
duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying project as ubdc-airbnb code repo above
themes: Inside Airbnb historical dump mirrors and archives (pre-2023 listings/calendar/reviews CSVs committed or released; archive.org mirrors referenced from GitHub)
Airbnb calendar / availability / blocked-night datasets and occupancy-estimation code (San Francisco model, review-to-booking ratios)
why_all: Documents exactly what a daily-calendar STR occupancy/income reconstruction looks like at sub-city geography (relevant to gap #2), even though we cannot pull the underlying files ourselves; worth citing as an existence proof and methodology reference, and as a reason to ask a human whether an academic-access request is worth pursuing before the pitch deadline (unlikely to clear in time).

Even though the raw store itself is gated, it documents exactly what a daily-calendar-scrape occupancy product looks like at scale (fields, geography, cadence) and is the dataset behind the peer-reviewed alternative to the San Francisco review-rate model — useful as a specification to replicate on our own calendars.
